selections.comment: Leading ARO trainer James Owen fields a couple of unexposed fillies in Piccadilly Lady and Hibikinada Du Mazet, both of whom are open to plenty of improvement. Also unexposed is Another Angel, who looked close to getting off the mark last time when burdened with top-weight. He should turn the tables with Aloof in this higher grade. However, in a trappy-looking contest, a chance is taken with JEEWAN. By a sire who was a world beater at this trip, he showed a surprising turn of foot here when placed over a mile behind decent horses and his jockey's claim is an added bonus.

selections.comment: The 118-rated SON OF ANARCHY gains marginal preference with his experience over obstacles. Gordon Elliott's charge won a maiden point by 15 lengths before running an encouraging race when fourth in a Punchestown maiden behind The Big Westerner on his hurdling debut. He's been disappointing since, but his recent second inspires more confidence and he can break his duck at the sixth attempt under Rules. Bumper winners Oneinthewell and Moon Eclipse have similar profiles as, after winning at Leopardstown on debut, neither figured in Listed company on their next start. The former has a great amount of potential based on his introduction when beating subsequent winner Eternal Echo. Moon Eclipse showed real promise, despite greenness, when coming from the rear to win on debut, but hasn't really progressed as perhaps expected and her recent hurdling debut offered minor encouragement. Cocovic took his form to a new level on his last start and may improve once more with the hood going back on.

selections.comment: REPORTER is a nicely bred horse who, on breeding, should be better than his current rating would suggest; however, he is clearly a free-going sort who does things his own way. A nice enough winner for the very first time at Windsor last time out, he only has a 4 lb raise in the weights to deal with here. He was always keeping on well in the closing stages, and that could very much help him land back-to-back contests here in what is a similar field to last time. Hint Of The Jungle was a decent enough 4th at Yarmouth last time and does have a 1 lb drop in the weights to help; he can take a step forward and place for the first time with his new yard here. And Over Spiced was in cracking form earlier this season, but the handicapper might have caught up with her. However, she is going well at present and can fill the places here.

And although Too Much Trevor is yet to win in 19 runs, he can fill the places here.

selections.comment: POLYGRAM is coming a bit frustrating to follow given the fact she has been a beaten favourite on the last two occasions; however, she was beaten by a horse (Cajole) who has since placed at Royal Ascot and in a Listed contest at Newcastle on her penultimate start, therefore she was unlucky to bounce into her. She was fairly beaten last time, but I would suggest drawing a line through that effort, as she is clearly better than that. This could present as the perfect opportunity for her to get her head in front for the very first time here, as this looks like a slightly easier contest than last time. Song N Dance was unlucky on debut at Wolverhampton in December, getting hampered at a bad time; she still managed to run on and claim 4th spot. She could have progressed nicely from 2 to 3; however, she might have to settle for a place finish here. And Seren Star is worth another look and could be one to run well here if settling better during her races.

Second, on all three of his starts, he makes his handicap debut off the mark of 70, which certainly does look workable, especially given the fact he has his second run since the gelding operation. He is sure to come on for the run from last time; therefore, he can get off the mark at the first attempt in handicap company. Saffredi wasn't beaten that far at all when coming 3rd last time out; he can go one better and place second here. And Connie's Rose can fill the places for Grace Harris, who has two runners in this race who could both do very well.

Makes Me Wonder is one of the only horses in this field to win a race, plus he came a decent 2nd last time out and therefore is in really good form at present; however, he might have to settle for another 2nd place finish here. And Electric Bass is getting slightly better with each run; he can fill the places here.

With a 3rd and 2nd in his last two runs, he has been running pretty well without winning at present, and now back down to his last winning mark, he could put that to good use and win this contest. The aforementioned Spirit Of The Bay comes from a yard that has landed the last two runnings on this race, but their runner here might have to settle for 2nd place here. And it is Carp Kid who has won this contest on the last two occasions; he hails from the John and Rhys Flint yard, who also train Spirit Of The Bay, and given their form in the previous race, their runners have to be taken very seriously; however, they might have to settle for place finishes this year.

Tex is also in very solid form and should be thereabouts again.

selections.comment: The 10f trip is a worry for OJ Lifestyle who is essentially a mile and though running well here last time did pull hard. He does like Epsom, but the slower pace up in trip is going to make him even harder to settle. In a very tight race, the ratings point marginally to ZARAKERJACK who is the least exposed of the quartet and who is suited by 10f and fast ground. The other two are both dangerous, Giselles Defence perhaps the most so. He is ultra-consistent, effective in the conditions and ran well at Newbury last time.

He is also progressing and the yard won the race last year. Gordon Grey is there other runner and he got his mojo back over hurdles last time after running poorly following a trip to race on the ice at St Moritz. He could easily make the frame again. One Cool Dreamer appeals as another to run in the first three. Very consistent on the Flat he ran well in a novice hurdle last time and ought to run to form here.

selections.comment: MAFNOOD ran well here last time making relentless late headway after having a lot to do 2f out. He ran his best race there since third here in April, clearly likes the track and reached a high on our ratings of 85 in 2024 (3lb better than he ran last time). Ridden a little closer to the action there is a chance he will return to that level and that would make him quite tough to beat. Revolutionise is in good form, will enjoy the going and distance and should go well. Similarly, Crimson Spirit who has won his last two. He looked all out at Brighton last time off a mark of 81 and the handicapper may have done for him here. He will probably start favourite making the other two a bit of value.

selections.comment: ROGUE SUPREMACY looks to hold the edge here having followed up a win on debut with two encouraging efforts in Listed company. The latest of those two runs when 5th of 7 can be upgraded a little as he was shuffled back at a key stage and would have been a bit closer. He looks very well-treated on handicap debut and can triumph for a second time. Soca Star looks the biggest danger having knocked on the door loudly last time. Steadily progressive John and Sean Quinn's filly is the only one in the field yet top taste success but can find a bit extra again and a mark of 74 loooks more than workable. Ice Cold Alex and Bleep Test both need to bounce back after modest efforts last time but both pose a threat if giving best. The former is marginally preferred

selections.comment: Top-weight MISS RAINBOW seeks a four-timer and will be difficult to stop. The hat-trick consisted of wins over 5f, 6f and 7f having dictated affairs in all three and she can control matters again. She doesn't appear to have reached her ceiling and is very much the one they all have to catch. Ski Angel may prove the biggest threat having rediscovered her best of late and with conditions spot on. Lady Of the Garr, Sixcor and Kyber Crstal all have claims but an improved effort from The Voominator could be on the cards now returned to turf and he's fancied to reach the frame ahead of that trio

selections.comment: SILENT CITY, Brielle and Wadacre Maestro stand out and should have this between them. Roger Varian's three year old Silent City looks the most solid option having taken a big step forward on second start last time to land a 1m maiden with some authourity on the back of heavy market support. Conditions suit again and there's likely more to come. Brielle is not far behind the selection of what she's achieved so far and shouldn't be too long in breaking her maiden but the drop back to 1m having gone so well over 1m4f last time tempers enthusiasm and Wadacre Maestro is preferred to give the selction most to do with the step up to 1m expected to bring further improvement from Charlie Johnston's gelding

selections.comment: A small but trappy affair where the progressive SALLAAL is taken to kick off his handicap career in style off a potentially lenient opening mark. A winner of two of his three runs, including over course and distance last time, and not disgraced in a Listed event in between them, Roger Varain's colt looks to have a bright future ahead and can confirm the promise here. Sailthisshipalone came close on second run this season last time and that effort was much more in keeping with the pick of his 2024 form. Although up 3lbs for that defeat he had slipped a bit in the handicap prior and looks more than capable off this kind of a mark. Ideally he'd prefer some cut but as long as it it's not rattling he should cope and represents the biggest danger to the selection. Rhythm Master is yet to score this term but has knocked on the door on many occasions and is next best

selections.comment: LUNAR ECLIPSE has a good opportunity to gain a second career win on fourth handicap start. A fine third last time off a break augurs well for the relatively unexposed four year old. She was a bit free that day over nine furlongs here but should have a better pace to aim at in this and can raise her game. Epidavros rarely fails to deliver her best and is knocking on the door loudly. Genuinely quick ground would be a concern but othwerwise shouldn't be far away. An improved effort could be on the cards from Hiromichi who is now 4lb below his last winning mark and gave a hint of better things to come with his best effort for a long while last time. He'll need to find a fair bit more but the forecast conditions suit (fast ground would be a concern) and he could make a big splash at decent odds

selections.comment: A poor affair but a few arrive in decent nick, none more so than GISELLES IZZY who gained her first win since last summer in a busy campaign since where she's tuimbled down the weights. Back in handicap company following her Classified Stakes win she'll find it tougher but she's capable of a bit better and is trusted to deliver the goods over a course and distance she's already won over. Rain Cap, also a course and distance winner (Superior Council is another), is a pretty relaible operator for this level and looks the most solid alternative. Jannas Journey is interesting dropped back to 6f having gone well the last twice over 7f. She's improved with each run this year, albeit from a very low starting point, and if coping with the drop back in trip poses a serious threat

selections.comment: Dubai Venture showed a tremendous attitude and improved a fair bit to land a double last time and should go close in persuit of a hat-trick off a 4lb higher mark. There could be more to come and if taking a similar step forward should take this but a chance is taken with TWOFORTHEGUTTER who is now a couple of pounds below his last winnng mark which came over course and sitance last June. Christopher Kellett's gelding will need to step up a bit on his latest run but that was still a decent effort given he weakened late in soft ground having dictated over 1m6f. The return to optimum conditions (both career wins came over CD) should spark some improvement and he can deny Dubai Venture the hat-trick. Last time out winner Crystal Guard commands respect but the admirably consistent Ebony Maw is feared a bit more. A big run from Come On John is on the cards upped in trip after finding 1m2f too sharp and, although probably best on AW, he can't be discounted

The former was a debut winner before chasing home the future Eclipse winner next time so is open to plenty of improvement on just his third start for all he may find this drop in trip unsuitable. The latter sets the form standard on his Wolferton runner up effort under a big weight. That can often be the strongest Listed contest of the season and he was a Group winner in the spring so is respected. Lord Massusus is a dual Listed winner including at this venue and though he is yet to prove quite up to winning at this level he could complete the tricast.

selections.comment: An open finale where it may be worth chancing hurdles winner LOS TOLDOS. He was beaten very early on his sole flat start for this yard but he looked unhappy on the soft ground that day and he's on a fair mark on his best UK form which came on fast ground. Another who will appreciate the quick ground as well as the drop in trip is Pearl Jewel who proved consistent until doing too much too soon from a poor draw last time in a hot race in the UK. She could bounce back down in grade back from a break while the progressive Tatum is also respected. She was a C&D winner in the spring before pulling clear with a progressive rival next time.
